items.title: Extend LoopStateEnum, add shared state-labels module, update CLI consumers
items.description:
Implement the status-vocabulary core+CLI change from spec 02 as ONE atomic increment (the enum addition compile-breaks the CLI's default-less statusExitCode, so core and CLI must land together to keep typecheck green). Steps:
1. packages/core/src/schemas.ts (~:228): append "REVIEWING" and "PAUSED_USAGE_LIMIT" to LoopStateEnumSchema (z.enum). Raw LoopStateStatusSchema (~:167) is unchanged.
2. NEW packages/core/src/state-labels.ts: export `type StateTone = "neutral"|"info"|"success"|"warning"|"danger"`; `interface StateLabel { label: string; tone: StateTone }`; `const STATE_LABELS: Record<LoopStateEnum, StateLabel>` with the exact label+tone table from spec 02 §2/§2.1 (PAUSED_HUMAN→{"Needs Human",warning}, REVIEWING→{"Reviewing",info}, PAUSED_USAGE_LIMIT→{"Usage Limit (Paused)",warning}, IDLE→{Idle,neutral}, RUNNING→{Running,info}, PAUSED→{Paused,info}, COMPLETE→{Complete,success}, LIMIT_REACHED→{"Limit Reached",warning}, ERROR→{Error,danger}, NOT_INSTALLED→{"Not Installed",neutral}, SLEEPING_LIMIT→{"Sleeping (Limit)",warning}, WEEKLY_LIMIT→{"Weekly Limit",warning}); `function getStateLabel(state): StateLabel`. Export the module from packages/core/src/index.ts.
3. packages/core/src/status.ts (~:106): change mapLoopStateStatus so `reviewing`→"REVIEWING" and `paused_usage_limit`→"PAUSED_USAGE_LIMIT" (keep the Record<LoopState["status"],LoopStateEnum> total over all 12 raw), and add `export` to the function; export it from index.ts too. Do NOT change deriveStatus/deriveFromStateJson logic — confirm the staleness branch keys on the RAW status, not the derived value, so REVIEWING is not swept into a downgrade.
4. packages/cli/src/status-commands.ts: refactor colorLoopState (~:538) to a tone map — `const TONE_COLOR: Record<StateTone,(s:string)=>string> = {neutral:c.dim, info:c.cyan, success:c.green, warning:c.yellow, danger:c.red}`; return `TONE_COLOR[STATE_LABELS[state].tone](state)`; REMOVE the `default:` branch (must be total). Extend statusExitCode (~:512, default-less switch): add `case "REVIEWING"` → ExitCode.RUNNING and `case "PAUSED_USAGE_LIMIT"` → ExitCode.LIMIT.
Tests: NEW packages/core/src/state-labels.test.ts (iterate LoopStateEnumSchema.options; assert every value has an entry, pin labels for the new/renamed states, getStateLabel never undefined); extend packages/core/src/status.test.ts (mapLoopStateStatus all 12 raw incl. the 2 remaps; deriveStatus yields REVIEWING/PAUSED_USAGE_LIMIT); extend packages/cli/src/status-commands.test.ts (statusExitCode REVIEWING→6, PAUSED_USAGE_LIMIT→4). Do NOT touch the web STATE_BADGE tables (item 002).
acceptanceCriteria: LoopStateEnumSchema includes REVIEWING and PAUSED_USAGE_LIMIT (12 derived values).
packages/core/src/state-labels.ts exports STATE_LABELS (total Record<LoopStateEnum,StateLabel>) + getStateLabel, both exported from the core index; labels/tones match spec 02 §2.1 (CANON §4.3).
mapLoopStateStatus is exported and maps reviewing→REVIEWING, paused_usage_limit→PAUSED_USAGE_LIMIT, with all 12 raw statuses mapped.
colorLoopState has no default: branch and routes through tone; statusExitCode maps REVIEWING→RUNNING(6) and PAUSED_USAGE_LIMIT→LIMIT(4) with no default:.
state-labels.test.ts asserts totality by iterating the enum; status.test.ts covers the 12-raw map + 2 deriveStatus cases; status-commands.test.ts covers the 2 exit codes.
pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm format:check && pnpm test passes
items.notes: Atomic per spec 02 §10 — enum addition breaks cli statusExitCode (default-less) until its cases are added, so core+cli land together. Web badge (Record<string>) still compiles (item 002). Tone table + exact labels are normative (CANON §4.3) — copy verbatim from spec 02 §2/§2.1. Gotcha: keep deriveFromStateJson staleness keyed on raw status (TRACEABILITY note #1).

In the moved file, change `import {findItemCommit,isTreeClean,gitCommit} from "@rauf/loop"` to relative imports `import {findItemCommit,isTreeClean} from "./git-reconcile.js"` and DROP gitCommit + the `node:child_process` spawn import (both only served the symbols that stay). Keep all @rauf/core imports as-is. Re-export the 5 functions + 5 types from packages/loop/src/index.ts. REDUCE packages/cli/src/recovery.ts to: keep the CLI-only --recover symbols (VerifyOutcome, VerifyRunner, defaultVerifyRunner, ItemRecoveryResult, reverifyAndCommitInterrupted — which imports gitCommit + type InterruptedItem from @rauf/loop), and re-export the moved symbols from @rauf/loop so existing ./recovery consumers keep compiling. Repoint packages/cli/src/resume-commands.ts and reset-commands.ts to import the moved symbols from @rauf/loop (keep reverifyAndCommitInterrupted/VerifyRunner from ./recovery.js). NO statement inside handleResume/handleReset changes. Trim unused @rauf/core imports in the reduced cli file. Move tests: packages/cli/src/recovery.test.ts → packages/loop/src/recovery.test.ts (its `from "./recovery.js"` import resolves to the loop copy after the move; no body change) and ADD two recoverInterruptedLoop unit cases (clean-tree no-op RecoverySummary: empty arrays/treeClean:true/stalledReset:0; a stalled in_progress item with no commit reset to pending with stalledReset incremented). Reduce packages/cli/src/recovery.test.ts to an import-smoke test (the re-exported moved symbols + the retained --recover symbols all resolve).

`grep -rn 'from "@rauf/cli"' packages/web/src` returns nothing (rule #1 intact).
The moved recovery tests pass in @rauf/loop including the 2 new recoverInterruptedLoop cases; packages/cli/src/recovery.test.ts is the reduced import-smoke.

items.title: Web recovery plumbing: startReviewLoop, assertNoLiveLoop guard, loop-defaults
items.description: Per spec 04 §6/§2.5 + 01 §6.2/§6.3. (1) Add `startReviewLoop(projectPath, options: LoopStartOptions)` to packages/web/src/server/loop-manager.ts beside startLoop (~:86): identical structure (resolveKey, the already-running dedupe guard, the LOOP_EVENT_TYPES subscription loop, promise tracking + map cleanup) but call `runner.startReviewOnly()` instead of `runner.start()`; return `{ok:true}|{ok:false,error:string}`. (2) NEW packages/web/src/server/routes/recovery-guard.ts exporting `assertNoLiveLoop(paths: BacklogPaths): Result<void>`: call core `checkLock(paths)` and return `err({code: ErrorCodes.LOCK_CONFLICT, message:"a loop is running on this backlog root — stop it first"})` when `lock.ok && lock.value.locked && lock.value.stale !== true`, else `ok(undefined)`; a checkLock IO error is fail-open (treated as not live). (3) NEW packages/web/src/server/loop-defaults.ts hoisting the loop default constants/helpers currently in packages/web/src/server/routes/loop.ts (~:54-87): DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES, DEFAULT_SESSION_TIMEOUT_MINUTES, resolveRequestMaxIterations; update loop.ts to import them from loop-defaults (delete the in-file duplicates — single source). Tests: extend packages/web/src/server/loop-manager.test.ts with a startReviewLoop describe (starts + tracks a review pass via the mock claude; rejects a duplicate start on the same backlog root).
acceptanceCriteria: LoopManager.startReviewLoop exists, mirrors startLoop, drives runner.startReviewOnly(), and dedupes on backlog root (second call returns {ok:false}).
packages/web/src/server/routes/recovery-guard.ts exports assertNoLiveLoop with the live/stale/fail-open semantics above.
packages/web/src/server/loop-defaults.ts holds the hoisted constants/helper and loop.ts imports them with no duplicated default values.

items.notes: Shared plumbing for the route items. startReviewLoop reuses the engine (REQ-WEB-08; runner unchanged). assertNoLiveLoop is the lightweight guard for unblock; reset/resume use acquire-and-hold from @rauf/loop (item 003) instead.

items.title: Web route: POST /:id/loop/review
items.description: Per spec 04 §5. Add `router.post("/:id/loop/review")` to packages/web/src/server/routes/loop.ts beside the loop-lifecycle routes. Preamble: `resolveProjectPath(id)` null→400 INVALID_ID; `validateProjectPath`→400 PATH_VIOLATION; parse ReviewBodySchema (spec 00 §7: `{model?, sessionTimeoutMinutes?, backlogRoot?}.strict()`) via safeParse→400 VALIDATION_ERROR; if body.backlogRoot, resolve via resolveBacklogRoot (→400 on !ok). Build `options = LoopStartOptionsSchema.parse({maxIterations:1, maxRetries:1, review:true, reviewOnly:true, sessionTimeoutMinutes: body.sessionTimeoutMinutes ?? DEFAULT_SESSION_TIMEOUT_MINUTES, model: body.model, backlogRoot})` — sessionTimeoutMinutes is REQUIRED by the schema; reuse DEFAULT_SESSION_TIMEOUT_MINUTES from loop-defaults (item 004). Call `getLoopManager().startReviewLoop(projectPath, options)`; on !ok return `errorResponse("CONFLICT", result.error)` with status 409; else `c.json({data:{started:true}})`. The route inherits the app-level CSRF middleware (403 without X-Rauf-Request — no per-route code). Tests: extend packages/web/src/server/routes/loop.test.ts with review cases (200 {started:true} via mock claude; 409 CONFLICT when a loop is already running via setupLongRunningClaude + a prior loop/start; 403 missing header; 400 invalid id a%2Fb; 400 non-numeric sessionTimeoutMinutes).
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/projects/:id/loop/review builds the review options (reviewOnly:true, required sessionTimeoutMinutes) and calls startReviewLoop, returning 200 {data:{started:true}}.
Returns 409 CONFLICT when a loop is already running for the backlog root; 403 without X-Rauf-Request; 400 for bad id/body.
loop.test.ts covers success/409/403/400 for the review route.
pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm format:check && pnpm test passes
items.notes: Review runs server-side; observed via the existing events SSE (Phase 1 read path). Guard is the start-path dedupe, not a recovery lock. Handler lives in loop.ts (01 §6.1).

items.title: Web routes: reset, backlog/unblock, backlog/validate (projects.ts)
items.description:
Per spec 04 §3/§7 + 00 §7/§8. In packages/web/src/server/routes/projects.ts add a local `recoveryErrorStatus(code)` helper (FILE_NOT_FOUND→404, LOCK_CONFLICT→409, IO_ERROR→500, VALIDATION_ERROR/INVALID_JSON→400, else 400) and colocate the body schemas ResetBodySchema/UnblockBodySchema (spec 00 §7, both `.strict()`). Register the unblock + validate routes BEFORE the existing `/:id/backlog/:itemId` routes (so "unblock"/"validate" are not captured as item IDs — mirror the restore/sweep precedent). Routes:
- `POST /:id/reset`: preamble (path/sandbox/ResetBodySchema/resolveBacklogPathsFromParam) → `acquireRecoveryLock(paths)` (from @rauf/loop, item 003); on !ok return 409 if LOCK_CONFLICT else 400 → `try { const r = resetProject(paths, {clearBacklog,keepProgress,keepLog}); if(!r.ok) return errorResponse(...) recoveryErrorStatus; c.json({data:r.value}) } finally { releaseRecoveryLock(paths) }`.
- `POST /:id/backlog/unblock`: preamble (UnblockBodySchema) → `assertNoLiveLoop(paths)` (recovery-guard, item 004); !ok→409 → `unblockItems(paths, body.itemId)` → map via recoveryErrorStatus; `c.json({data:result.value})` ({unblockedCount,unblockedIds}).
- `GET /:id/backlog/validate`: preamble (no body; `?backlogRoot` query via resolveBacklogPathsFromParam) → `validateBacklog(paths,{})` → map via recoveryErrorStatus; `c.json({data:result.value})` ({valid,findings}). NO CSRF/lock guard (read-only GET).
Tests: NEW packages/web/src/server/routes/recovery.test.ts copying the loop.test.ts harness (vi.hoisted HOME redirect, createProject, setupMockClaude, resetLoopManager, ACTIVE_DIR cleanup) plus the seedLiveLock + seedState helpers from spec 06 §3.0. Cover reset (200/403/409-live/404/400), unblock (200 all + by-id/403/409-live/404/400), validate (200 valid/200 findings DUPLICATE_ID/safe-during-live-run/no-CSRF-required/404/400 sandbox backlogRoot), plus a route-mounting smoke (POST reset/resume/unblock → 403 not 404).
acceptanceCriteria: The three routes exist in projects.ts, with unblock/validate registered before /:id/backlog/:itemId, wrapping resetProject/unblockItems/validateBacklog.
reset is acquire-and-hold guarded (409 on live lock; lock released in finally); unblock uses assertNoLiveLoop (409 on live); validate is GET, read-only, ungated, needs no CSRF header.
Result→HTTP mapping uses recoveryErrorStatus; success envelopes match spec 00 §5; validate findings return 200 with valid:false (not an HTTP error).
recovery.test.ts covers the success/403/409/404/400 matrix for the three routes plus validate's read-only cases and the mounting smoke.
pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm format:check && pnpm test passes
items.notes: Body schemas from spec 00 §7. 403 is inherited app-level CSRF (no per-route code). Live-lock fixture: write .loop.lock {pid: process.pid, startedAt, processStartTime: null} so checkLock/acquireRecoveryLock report live (spec 06 §3.0).

items.title: Web route: POST /:id/resume (reconcile + relaunch)
items.description: Per spec 04 §4 + 00 §6/§7. Add `router.post("/:id/resume")` to packages/web/src/server/routes/projects.ts (after item 006's routes; reuse its recoveryErrorStatus helper). Preamble with ResumeBodySchema (spec 00 §7: `{backlogRoot?, retryBlocked?, answers?: {itemId,text}[]}.strict()`). Then `acquireRecoveryLock(paths)` (from @rauf/loop); !ok→409 if LOCK_CONFLICT else 400. Inside `try`: (a) for each `{itemId,text}` in `body.answers ?? []`, `updateItem(paths, itemId, {humanAnswer: text, status:"pending", needsHuman:false, blockedReason:null})` (OQ-T2: the request field is `text`, written as humanAnswer); map errors via recoveryErrorStatus. (b) if `body.retryBlocked`, `unblockItems(paths)`. (c) `const recovery = await recoverInterruptedLoop(paths)` (async, from @rauf/loop); !ok→map error. (d) if `recovery.value.interrupted.length>0` → set reason="…run `rauf resume --recover` from the CLI…", relaunch=false; else read backlog (readBacklog) and if `selectNextItem(...)===null` → reason="no eligible items", relaunch=false; else relaunch=true + build `relaunchOptions = LoopStartOptionsSchema.parse({maxIterations: resolveRequestMaxIterations(...), maxRetries: DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES, sessionTimeoutMinutes: DEFAULT_SESSION_TIMEOUT_MINUTES, backlogRoot})` (from loop-defaults, item 004). `finally { releaseRecoveryLock(paths) }`. AFTER the try/finally (lock released), if relaunch && relaunchOptions: `const started = loopManager.startLoop(projectPath, relaunchOptions); relaunched = started.ok; if(!started.ok) reason = started.error`. Return `c.json({data: {reconciled, relaunched, reason} as ResumeResult})`. The --recover reverify+commit path is CLI-only and is NOT exposed here. Tests: add resume cases to packages/web/src/server/routes/recovery.test.ts (200 relaunched:false when nothing eligible; 200 relaunched:true with a pending item + setupLongRunningClaude; answers injection {itemId,text} unblocks the item to pending; 403; 409-live; 404; 400 malformed answers missing text; regression: a relaunched resume leaves no orphaned recovery lock so a second resume is not 409'd after stopLoop/shutdownAll).
acceptanceCriteria: POST /:id/resume acquires-and-holds the lock, injects answers (text→humanAnswer), honors retryBlocked, awaits recoverInterruptedLoop, decides relaunch, releases the lock in finally BEFORE the relaunch, then calls loopManager.startLoop.

Returns 200 {data: ResumeResult {reconciled, relaunched, reason?}}; 409 on live lock; 403/404/400 as specified; interrupted-uncommitted work surfaces in reason with relaunched:false (no --recover on web).
A failed relaunch is reported as relaunched:false + reason in a 200 (not an HTTP error).
recovery.test.ts resume cases pass including the OQ-T2 answers test and the no-orphaned-lock regression.
pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm format:check && pnpm test passes
items.notes: Mirrors CLI resume-commands.ts:268-424 minus --recover. Lock released before relaunch so the loop's own lock acquisition succeeds. Same projects.ts file as item 006 (ordering dependency).

items.title: Frontend: status-page Recovery control group
items.description: Per spec 04 §8. In packages/web/src/client/routes/projects/status.tsx add a "Recovery" control group near the existing Start/Stop controls (~:997-1027), using the existing TanStack Query + raufFetch patterns (raufFetch injects X-Rauf-Request on mutations — verify; pass it explicitly if it does not for these POSTs). Five controls: Reset (POST /reset, behind a confirm dialog), Resume (POST /resume), Review (POST /loop/review), Unblock (POST /backlog/unblock), Validate (GET /backlog/validate as a useQuery with enabled:false + a refetch button). Add recoveryMessage + validationResult + confirmReset React state. Each mutation onSuccess sets a friendly recoveryMessage (e.g. `Unblocked ${data.unblockedCount} item(s)`, `Reset complete — …`, resume `relaunched ? "Resumed — loop relaunched" : reason`), clears loopError, and invalidates ["projects", projectId]; onError sets loopError. A shared `recoveryErrorMessage(res)` maps 409→"a loop is running — stop it first" else the body error message. Render recoveryMessage in a dismissible banner mirroring the existing loopError banner (~:1031-1048); render validationResult as "Backlog is valid" or a severity-toned findings list. Apply applicability-based disabling per spec 04 §8.7 (Resume enabled for PAUSED/PAUSED_HUMAN/PAUSED_USAGE_LIMIT/ERROR/IDLE with non-done work; Review disabled while RUNNING/REVIEWING/STARTING; Unblock enabled when backlogSummary.blocked>0; Validate always; Reset confirm-gated). No React test harness (REQ-TEST-03) — behavior is covered by the backend route tests + core unit tests.
acceptanceCriteria: status.tsx shows a Recovery group with Reset (confirm)/Resume/Review/Unblock/Validate wired to the 5 endpoints, sending X-Rauf-Request on the POSTs.
Each action surfaces a result message; a 409 renders "a loop is running — stop it first"; validate renders the findings list / valid state.
Controls disable per the spec 04 §8.7 applicability table, using the derived loopState (incl. REVIEWING/PAUSED_USAGE_LIMIT).
pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm format:check && pnpm test passes; no *.test.tsx added
items.notes: Disabling is UX only — the backend still enforces every guard. No component tests (REQ-TEST-03); the route tests + core unit tests are the coverage.
